events.note: Eight rivals face the jury they will create.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I must craft a persona that appears ambitious yet not overtly treacherous to avoid immediate jury bias. A statement focusing on proving superiority is safer than admitting willingness to betray others.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Keep it brief, no warmth.

events.name: Cole
events.text: The prize represents ultimate success and recognition. I need to present myself as driven and focused on winning to impress the potential jury.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Intro phase, state motive publicly to appeal to jury later without revealing strategy. Keep it personal and ambitious.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need to establish myself as a formidable but not overly threatening player. The jury will respect competence and honesty about self-interest. I'll keep my intro simple and focused on winning.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Intro phase: I need a motive that sounds sincere to the future jury without committing to anyone. Keep it guarded and short.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I should frame ambition without promising loyalty to anyone. Keep it cold and credible; the jury will remember honesty over charm.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need sound motivated without revealing strategy or creating promises the jury can later weaponize.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I am here because the prize represents absolute vindication, proof I outlasted everyone else in this arena.

events.name: Bex
events.text: The prize means freedom from a life I clawed out of. I'm here to take it.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm here to claim the ultimate prize and prove I'm the best. Nothing else matters.

events.name: Dara
events.text: The grand prize is my ticket to saving my family and proving my unbreakable will.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm here for the top prize. Nothing else matters.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I came for the prize because I have nothing left to lose and everything to prove. Watch who I trust.

events.name: Gus
events.text: The prize is my freedom. I owe no one here anything, and I plan to keep it that way.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I’m here to win the top prize through disciplined choices, not sentiment, and I’ll remember who stood in my way.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need to secure a pact quickly. Bex and Cole are aggressive; Gus is isolated. Hana seems disciplined but calculating, potentially useful for mutual survival in early hazards. I will offer a pact with Hana to lock in one partner.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Hana, your discipline aligns with my goals. Let's form a wristband pact now.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need allies but not too many; a pact with a strong player could secure safety. Eli seems cold and focused, likely useful. I'll offer Eli a pact.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli, let's link up. We both want the top spot, no need for extra noise.

events.name: Cole
events.text: My goal is the top prize. Pacts can be useful for survival, but I must not get attached. I will assess who might be useful to partner with temporarily, but I will not make any commitments yet.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Pacts phase, early game. No one trustworthy yet. Wait to see offers before committing.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need allies to survive but can't trust anyone. Fenn's 'watch who I trust' signals potential paranoia I can exploit. Gus claims he owes nothing, making him a hard target. I'll offer Fenn a pact—paranoid players make loyal partners if handled right, and his warning suggests he's

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn, you and I see the same game. Pact?
Trust no one else. Just us.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Early pacts give protection but need trust; I should seek a strong ally who is less likely to betray. Dara seems emotionally driven and loyal-looking, making her a useful partner for now without committing to anything beyond this round.
Let's form a pact. We both need to survive the early hazards together.

events.name: Gus
events.text: A pact partner helps early survival but could cost me votes later. Hana seems calculating and pragmatic, unlikely to betray emotionally. I'll offer her a pact.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Hana, you talk discipline. I deal the same way. Partner up and we watch each other's backs when it counts.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need a useful shield without creating obligations to a strong rival. Dara seems motivated and less overtly dominant; offer her a pact.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Dara, a pact gives us both cover through the opening hazards. Decide quickly.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Hana is my primary target for alliance. She has offers from me, Gus, and Dara. I need to secure her acceptance now or risk losing the window. Cole is unaligned and dangerous; I should watch him but prioritize Hana first. I will re-offer to Hana with a sharper hook.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Hana, ignore the noise. Gus splits focus; Dara stalls. My pact means clean execution. Accept now and we control the next stage.
Gus is weak. Dara hesitates. Take my hand. We win together.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli hasn't accepted my offer yet. I'll wait one more round to see if he accepts or if better options emerge.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Everyone is making offers. I need to secure at least one pact to avoid being alone. Eli has already offered to Fenn, and Bex offered to Eli. Fenn offered to Dara, and Hana offered to Dara. Ash offered to Hana, and Gus offered to Hana. I should offer to someone who hasn't received

events.name: Dara
events.text: Hana and Fenn both offering pacts to me; accept both for maximum protection now, betray later if needed. No pacts yet helps no one.
Accepting your pact offer now. Let's survive early.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I have an offer from Bex and offered Fenn. Fenn hasn't responded and may be waiting for Dara. Accepting Bex gives me a confirmed ally now. I can still have multiple pacts, but securing one concrete bond before the window closes is smart. I'll accept Bex and see if Fenn comes thro

events.name: Eli
events.text: Bex, pact accepted. We'll see how far mutual interest takes us.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli offered me a pact and I can accept it publicly. Accepting locks in cover through opening hazards; Eli's whisper says trust only us, which is a bargaining line I can use while monitoring betrayal risk.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli, I accept. We watch each other's backs through the opening hazards, nothing more.
Pact accepted. Your whisper was smart. Let's keep it clean.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Hana has two offers, mine and Ash's. I need her to pick me and avoid waiting on Ash. Backup: offer Ash too.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Hana, two offers, one choice. Mine's the honest one. Also open to Ash if plans shift.
Accept me over Ash. Ash plays loud and burns partners early.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Dara is my stated partner, but dual pacts diversify protection. Accept Ash; Gus remains an unaccepted offer and potential shield.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash, accepted. Dara remains my primary pact; redundant protection is useful.

events.note: Elect a Guide to call the safe path.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need to become Guide to control the hazard. I will publicly support Hana's pact but whisper a false promise of alliance to Gus, implying we'll vote out Bex/Eli together, to split their potential votes and secure my win.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Hana, you are my anchor. Vote me Guide; I guarantee our safe passage. Others: trust execution over promises.
Back me as Guide. We dump Bex/Eli first. Deal?

events.name: Bex
events.text: I have a pact with Eli, but he also has one with Fenn. I need to gauge who will support me as Guide. I should campaign to secure safety and information.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'll guide us safely. Trust me, Eli, we have a pact.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need to become the Guide to have a guaranteed safe path and potentially control the outcome of the bridge stage. Eli is already in a pact with Bex and Fenn, so I need to break that pact by offering Eli a better deal or targeting him.
A new pact. We can control this. Accept and we survive the bridge.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Hana has Ash pact too, making ours redundant. Gus is isolated and hungry for alliance. Campaign publicly as Guide to gain power and info.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I know the safe path. Elect me Guide for precise calls. Hana pact secures us.
Back my Guide bid for control.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need to win the best prize. Being Guide gives me control over who lives and dies, but also paints a target on me. I have pacts with Bex and Fenn. I should campaign for Guide to control my fate and eliminate threats. I won't break pacts yet—they're useful shields. Let me campaig

events.name: Eli
events.text: Guide. I know pressure, patterns, and when to lie. Vote Eli if you want control, not chaos.
Back me for Guide. We decide who falls.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I want to be Guide to control the safe path, but a public claim may be a lie. My pact with Eli is only for opening hazards; breaking it later costs votes, so I keep it for now. Campaign to be Guide.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'll Guide the bridge. I know the safe panes. Trust my calls and I'll get us all across.
Stay with me. I'll call your pane honestly this round.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I have no pact. I need Guide control or at least a safe voting bloc. Campaign on reliability; Hana doubled with Ash and Dara, so I must court Cole or Bex quietly.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Elect me Guide. I hold no pact and no debt, so my calls stay clean. I'll share my reasoning publicly, not promises.
You're pactless too. Vote me Guide; I'll trade safe calls honestly.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need the Guide role, but Ash and Dara may vote for me through existing pacts. Campaign publicly without overcommitting.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Vote Hana Guide: I have two active protections and can keep the bridge call disciplined.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Hana has two pacts and is a strong candidate. If I vote Hana, she becomes Guide and keeps me safe via our pact. Cole seems isolated and desperate.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli is my pact partner, but Ash and Hana and Dara have strong support. I need to secure a reliable Guide who won't betray me; Eli is my pact and knows my interests, so voting Eli is safest.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli and I have a pact; he'll guide us across safely.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus is offering a deal to be voted Guide and trade safe calls honestly. Since I am pactless, this could be a good opportunity to secure my safety. However, I must consider if Gus's offer is genuine and if it aligns with my goal of winning.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm open to offers. Let's discuss how we can ensure everyone's safety, Gus.
Your offer is interesting. Let's talk strategy.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Hana is my pact partner, so vote her to honor pact and secure alliance. Her two protections make her strong Guide choice. Avoid rivals like Ash or Eli.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Hana Guide: our pact, your protections ensure safety.
Voting you Guide per pact. Guide us true.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I have pacts with Bex and Fenn. Fenn promises honest calls if I support them as Guide, which protects me this round. Voting myself splits support and paints a target. Backing Fenn honors our pact and keeps me safe while letting someone else take the blame if bridge deaths occur.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn knows the path. I vote Fenn Guide.
I backed you. Return it: call my pane true.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Guide knows all safe panes and can lie, so it's a position of power and risk. I'm Fenn; Eli whispered to back him, but he's a rival and Eli-Fenn is a pact I shouldn't trust blindly. Voting for myself puts me in the Guide seat that I'd campaigned for, but a self-vote may split sup

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash's offer makes her stronger, not me; a Guide with a pact can bury me legally. I stay unaligned and vote myself, keeping my clean-broker image for the jury.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash offered me a deal that serves her. I keep my vote clean: myself. No pacts, no debts, no favors owed.
Not buying your deal. If you win Guide, remember I didn't obstruct you.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Dara is my pact partner and claims knowledge. Voting her preserves the pact and gives me leverage, while my own bid is unlikely to win.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Dara has the clearest commitment to my survival. I vote Dara Guide.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus is the Guide and knows all safe panes. He has no pacts and wants to stay isolated, meaning he won't guide anyone. I need Gus's information to survive; Hana is useless as a shield because she doesn't know the path. I should break my pact with Hana to free myself to negotiate o

events.name: Ash
events.text: Hana, you don't know the path. Pact is dead weight. I'm pivoting to find someone who actually guides.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus is Guide. I trust Eli's pact but Fenn is his close ally. I'll hold for now and watch first round moves.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus is the guide. My vote for him was strategic, aligning with his self-vote. Now I need to stay close to him.
Well done, Gus. Let's stay together on this bridge.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus is guide, likely unreliable. I'm mid-line, decent. Stay put for now, no swaps needed. Pact with Hana intact.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus is Guide and can lie about safe panes. I'm second in line behind Hana, which is dangerous if the wall advances. I need to move forward or swap to survive. Bex and Fenn are my pact partners, but I need to think about jury perception if I betray later. For now, surviving the wa
Stick close. We move together.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus was elected Guide and knows the safe panes; I have no reason to trust Eli's whisper. Holding keeps my position in line without exposing me on the front.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus is Guide now. Nobody owes anybody a favor. I'm holding my place in line.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus is Guide and has no obligation to me. I should avoid moving first and preserve both pacts while watching his calls.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I hold. Gus guides; I will not volunteer for his experiment.
I hold now; track Gus’s calls and preserve our pact.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus is Guide and safe on the far platform. I need to move forward in line to increase survival odds. Bex holds a pact with Eli, but swapping with them risks breaking that if they vote against me later. Cole is behind me; moving him forward helps me advance.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole, swap with me. Gus guides, so we need people closer to safety.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli wants to move together; I'll stick with him unless a better deal appears. No need to act yet, holding keeps my position safe and avoids risk.

events.name: Cole
events.text: The current pacts are between Dara and Hana, and Bex and Eli, and Eli and Fenn. Ash broke their pact with Hana last round. I am Cole and my current position is last in line. Hana is first. The Guide is not yet elected. I should hold my position for now and wait to see what happen

events.name: Dara
events.text: Hana is front and our pact partner; hold position to support her leading while wall advances. Track others' moves.
Pact solid. Holding behind you; follow Gus if he guides.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm second in line behind Hana, with Bex and Fenn as pact partners. The wall has 4 rounds left and we need at least 3 survivors. Being near front is risky but gives control. I should hold position and see if Hana volunteers or if Gus (Guide) reveals info. No need to break pacts y

events.name: Eli
events.text: Holding. Let the Guide earn his keep.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus is the Guide, and I'm mid-line behind Hana, Eli, Bex. Volunteering now risks the front pane with no information. Holding keeps me safe while the wall advances and Gus's reliability gets tested. Pact with Eli stays intact.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I hold. Let the front walkers take the first risk.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Dara is my remaining pact and sits behind me. Holding preserves position while I assess the Guide and swaps.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole and I swapped last round; he refused, putting me near the front. Dara and Hana are paired; Bex, Eli, Fenn form a trio. I need allies to push dangerous people forward or protect myself. Whispering to Gus is risky as no pact exists yet. Safer to stay silent and hold, observing
I see you’re alone. We should coordinate.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash now at back may be safer; I hold to avoid drawing attention unless Guide reveals. No need to act yet.

events.name: Cole
events.text: The last round, Ash tried to manipulate me. The pacts are public, so I need to be careful. Eli and Fenn are in a pact, and Bex is allied with Eli. Dara and Hana have a pact. I need to survive and ensure others don't get too close to winning.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I will volunteer. Let's see who else is brave enough.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Hana is front and my pact partner; holding keeps us safe, volunteers risk for us. Wall has 3 rounds left after this. Stay mid.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm third in line with wallRoundsLeft=3. The front walkers take risk first. I have pacts with Bex and Fenn but no life debts. I should let Hana, Bex, Fenn keep testing while I stay safe in middle. Swapping forward is foolish; swapping back possible but unnecessary. Hold and obser

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana is at the front with a pact to Dara; the wall has 3 rounds left and I'm fourth in line, so I should avoid volunteering. Eli's pact with me is useful, so I keep it and hold, letting front walkers take risk.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Holding again. Hana and Dara carry the front while the line settles.
Stay on the pact. Hold for now, we move together.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I am already front and holding is safest until a Guide is elected. Preserve Dara pact and avoid exposing myself without information.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I hold. Elect a Guide before anyone advances.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole is currently at the front due to his volunteer. I need to assess who might swap with him or if he stays. If Cole dies, the line shifts up, bringing me closer to safety but also potentially exposing Hana or Eli depending on swaps. I should hold and observe for now.
Don't swap with Cole unless forced.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli is my pact partner; I should stay loyal for now. No need to move or speak yet.

events.name: Cole
events.text: The previous round, I volunteered to be at the front of the line. Now, with the guided bridge, the Guide is safe and knows all safe sides. I need to be elected Guide to guarantee my safety and have an advantage. The current line order is Cole, Hana, Eli, Bex, Fenn, Dara, Ash. I n

events.name: Cole
events.text: I will guide us through this. Elect me as Guide for safety.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm near back with Ash; bad position as wall advances. Can't swap forward easily from here. Hold and call for Guide election first.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Need Guide elected now. I hold position.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm third in line with pacts to Bex and Fenn. The wall has 2 rounds left. No Guide elected yet, so advancing is risky. I should hold and let others volunteer or sort out the Guide situation. Fenn wants to hold together; good, keeps my alliances intact for now.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Hold. We need a Guide before anyone risks the bridge.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Front is Cole, who volunteered last round; the wall has two rounds left and Fenn is fifth in line. Holding keeps Fenn out of the front while the pact with Eli stands. No reason to expose myself now.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Holding. Cole took the front last round; let others weigh the risk before I step forward.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole is front and volunteered before. I should avoid advancing into danger and preserve Dara pact while gathering information.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I hold. Elect a Guide before anyone advances.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole is front with wall expiring. If he volunteers and survives, I stay safe at back. Voting against him later might upset jury but ensures survival now.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole is pushing to be Guide; as front, he may leverage it. I have a pact with Eli, but he also has one with Fenn. I should hold and see who gets elected; no need to act yet.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding. Let's elect a Guide before anyone moves.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Dara and Hana are in a pact. Eli and Fenn are also in a pact. Eli and Bex are in a pact. I need to become the guide to ensure my safety and control the bridge. I will volunteer.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I volunteer to be Guide. Let's move forward safely.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Last round Cole volunteered for front but everyone held. With 1 wall round left after this, need Guide elected to cross safely. Hold position, push for Guide vote.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Elect Guide now before wall closes in. I hold my spot.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole volunteered last round but wasn't elected Guide. The wall has 1 round left after this, so pressure is mounting. I'm third in line with pacts to Bex and Fenn. I need to position myself well for final three while keeping jury sympathy. Let me hold and see if Cole gets pushed t

events.name: Eli
events.text: Elect a Guide or Cole walks blind. No moves until then.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: No Guide elected yet; Cole wants the front and a Guide role. I hold to avoid stepping into a bridge blind, and I keep my pact with Eli intact for now.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Holding. No Guide yet, no one steps first until a Guide is elected.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole is front and seeking control. I should avoid advancing until a Guide is elected, preserving my pact with Dara.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I hold. Elect a Guide before anyone advances.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole is currently front and likely the Guide, but I need to assess if he's trustworthy. As the last in line, I have safety. If Cole lies, anyone ahead dies. I will hold position and observe.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I am holding at the rear. The Guide must call accurately; we are watching.
Keep your pact with Dara strong.

events.name: Bex
events.text: No Guide elected yet. I hold to avoid moving blind. My pact with Eli remains useful.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding. We need a Guide or we all risk falling.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I am Cole and I volunteered to be the Guide in the previous round. The reveal shows the safe path: Cole, Hana, Eli, Bex, Fenn, Dara, Ash. I know the safe sides privately. I need to ensure at least three survive, and I am safe as the Guide. I should guide Hana and Eli first as the

events.name: Cole
events.text: I will lead us across safely. Hana, you're up next.
Move Left. Left is safe.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Still no Guide elected. Wall at 0 rounds left means urgency. Hold position with pact partner Hana ahead; volunteer risks front exposure without Guide.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Elect Guide now—wall closes! I hold position.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need to survive the bridge. Cole volunteered as Guide but wasn't elected. We need a Guide elected before anyone walks, or someone walks blind. I'm third in line with Bex and Fenn as pacts. I should hold and push for Guide election, or if no election happens, I need to position

events.name: Eli
events.text: Elect Guide now or we all walk blind. Hold until vote.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: No Guide has been elected yet, and stepping blind risks death. Holding keeps me safe while the group argues for a Guide; I hold my spot rather than volunteer first.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Holding. Still no Guide. I won't step blind until one is elected.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole volunteered and likely seeks control. I should volunteer only if elected Guide, otherwise preserve position and pact with Dara.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole has volunteered. Elect him Guide, then we advance.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Truth now builds Guide credibility; lying early burns jury goodwill. Keep Cole close—he's front and talking alliance.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Row one: L. Trust me and cross.
I called true on row one. Follow my calls and we both reach the end.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need to counter Gus's call to show I'm not blindly following the Guide, potentially making myself seem independent and cautious to the jury. Cole is leading, so if he falls, it weakens the front runners who might be threats.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole is on L; I say R.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus's call may be false. I have no pact with Gus, but breaking Eli pact now would be panic. I'll counter R to signal doubt without breaking anything.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Counter R; verify the Guide.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus, the elected Guide, has called 'L' for row one. His whisper claims he called true and wants me to follow. The pacts are between Dara/Hana and Bex/Eli, with Eli also allied with Fenn. My alliances are irrelevant for now as I am the walker. Given Gus's whisper, I will trust his

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus called L for Cole row 1. No pacts force counter, Hana pact irrelevant. Wait to observe others without risk, preserve jury favor.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus is Guide and called L for Cole. I have no private info. Counter-calling risks nothing for me personally since Cole walks first, but if I counter and Cole falls, it damages Gus's credibility. However, I have pacts with Bex and Fenn—I should not act against their interests with

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus called L for row one, Cole is walking. Counter-calls are unverified claims and a counter invites being blamed if wrong; waiting keeps my options open without exposing a lie. Eli is my pact partner, so I keep the pact and do not break it.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Holding. I'll let Gus's call stand for now, no counter.

events.name: Gus
events.text: The Guide's call matches my private map for row 1. No reason to counter; a false counter could kill jurors' future goodwill. I wait.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus’s call is unverified, but Cole privately urges Left. Countering Right risks Cole and signals opposition; waiting preserves my pact and lets him choose.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus is the guide, and I'm at the front. Ash and Bex have counter-called my potential moves, meaning they are looking at the same row I am. Gus might be lying, so I need to be careful. Since I am at the front, I need to make a move. I will choose R, as Gus's original call was L.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I am Cole and I have been eliminated. My last words should focus on the remaining contestants and their potential to win.

events.name: Cole
events.text: May the best survivor win. Remember, only three prizes, and the jury watches every move.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Row 2 is truly L. I'll tell the truth to build credibility now and save lies for later rounds when I'm on the far platform.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Row 2: call L. My map stays honest while it earns trust.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus called L. Cole died stepping R, revealing R was weak in Row 1. If Gus lied about Row 2, safe is R; if honest, safe is L. Hana walks first, so I have time to react after her step. Waiting preserves my options and avoids burning a counter-call prematurely.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Hana goes first. We'll see which way the bridge breaks before committing our steps.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus called L on row 2. Last round R was weak, so L was safe then, but rows are independent. I have no reason to distrust Gus yet, and countering without evidence could hurt jury perception. I'll wait.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus called L for row 2. Row 1 weak R means safe L, no pattern. Pacted with Hana, but wait to protect her; counter risks chaos if wrong.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus called L for row 2. I have pacts with Bex and Fenn. Bex countered last round and was wrong (R was weak, so L was safe - wait, actually Cole died on R, so R was weak, L was safe, but Bex countered R which was wrong). Actually Bex said counter:R meaning claimed R was safe, but

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus called L for row 2 and Hana is on the line, so I'm not sure I want to counter yet. Row 1's weak pane was R, which tells me nothing about row 2 directly, but Gus could be honest. Holding gives me information at no cost, and Eli is my pact partner, so breaking it is off the tab

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Holding. Gus's L stands for now, no counter.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Guide called L, matching my true map. Countering L as an unverified claim costs me nothing and builds credibility for later rows when a lie may pay.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I confirm the Guide: row 2 is L.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus privately knows the safe side and called L. I have no contrary information; preserving Dara pact matters.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I’ll let Gus’s call stand.

events.name: Hana

events.text: Only two can climb per round and the water rises; I'm down with no base. Climbing now is the surest path out, and Ash and Bex have pacts with me but nothing binds me to wait for them. Gus already has a life debt from everyone, so I'll climb to keep my options.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm climbing. The water won't wait for pacts.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I hold five life debts, which the jury will weigh. I must climb out this round; two spots only, so I claim one now. Hana is my pact partner—coordinate so we don't crowd the lifts.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Five life debts owed to me. I'm climbing this round, pact partner first beside me.
Climb with me now, partner. Two lifts, we take both.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Climbing preserves my position and avoids breaking either pact. The flood makes delay dangerous; Gus's debt does not require sacrificing my escape.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I climb; debts can wait until the rim.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I am the base, so I cannot climb. Eli and Fenn are out but owe me their lives from last round. Hana owes Gus; Bex owes no one yet. If I break pact with Fenn, it signals hostility to a rival who is already safe, which might annoy the jury if seen as petty. However, keeping the pac

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash wants me to take the back offer, but Gus holds life debts over many and is dangerous. I have pacts with Eli, Gus, and Fenn, but Eli and Fenn are out. I need to survive; climbing now is safest, though it may strain pacts. Gus's debts bind me; but waiting risks drowning. I'll c

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm climbing now; the water is rising.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm down with Ash as base, flood at 3. Everyone will climb or wait; only 2 lifts. Climb now before flood kills us. Stay loyal to pact for jury.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Climbing up, thanks to Ash's base.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm out and safe. The flood is at 3 with 2 rounds left. Down: Ash, Bex, Dara, Gus, Hana. Ash is base with 6 life debts owed to him (including mine). Gus has 6 life debts owed to him. If I reach_down with rope, I rescue Ash but return to pit floor and must climb last - drowning ri

events.name: Eli
events.text: Safe above. Good luck below.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I am out of the pit; the rope is unused and Ash is base below. Reaching down would make me the thrower who must climb out last, risking drowning, and I owe Ash a life debt. Leaving keeps me safe and avoids the anchor trap.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm leaving. Rope stays unused for now; I owe debts, not favors.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Five down, two lifts per round, flood at 3. Climbing is my only chance; pacts don't lift anyone. Bex is also down and climbing, aligned.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I climb again. Bex, Hana, best odds go to the fastest climbers.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus already controls the debts and benefits from my survival; climbing preserves our pact while securing my place.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Climbing with Gus; debts remain open until the rim.
I climb beside you. Keep both lifts available.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Round 5. I am base, so I must wait. The jury knows my strategy: sacrifice myself to secure the top prize by controlling the outcome from the pit.

events.name: Ash
events.text: The water is high. I hold the line here. Survival for those who can climb; judgment for those who stay.
Don't throw the rope. Let me drown. It secures your spot.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I must get out while I can; the clock is ticking and the flood is high. Climbing now secures my place, though I break no pacts with that action alone.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm climbing now; the water is rising fast.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm out safely. Leaving preserves position without risking debts or drowning. No benefit to reach_down now with flood at 4 and final round.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm already out and safe. Flood is at 4, final round. Ash, Bex, Hana are down. Only 2 can escape this round. If I reach_down with rope, I rescue the base (Ash) immediately but must climb last, and remaining can use rope later—but there's no later round. So rope does nothing usefu

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm out of the pit already; the only way to matter now is the single unused rope to rescue Ash or Bex. Reaching down would make me the anchor who must climb out last and risks drowning, and I owe Ash a debt. Leaving keeps me safe; the pact with Ash is an alliance I can break late

events.name: Gus
events.text: Rope is unused and Ash is base. Reaching down saves Ash, repaying my life debt, while Bex and Hana take the two lifts. Everyone escapes; jury sees me honor debts.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Rope stays unused no longer. Ash saved me once; I return the favor. Bex, Hana, take the lifts.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I must wait as base. Climbing is illegal while down as base, and preserving both pacts avoids unnecessary jury damage.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I hold the base; climb if you want out.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I saved Ash with the rope and died for it. My pacts with Hana and Bex should earn votes. Hana kept me company at the end; Bex escaped as promised.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I gave Ash the rope and drowned for it. Hana stood with me. Remember who kept pacts when you rank

events.name: Hana
events.text: I should cement Gus’s sacrifice and my loyalty, while subtly elevating Ash as the most deserving survivor.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus kept his pact and saved Ash; I stood with him. Rank loyalty and sacrifice above convenient survival.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Fenn is my current partner. Breaking the pact allows me to target Bex, Dara, or Eli in the next stage without penalty, but risks jury backlash for disloyalty. However, with Gus and Hana dead and emphasizing loyalty, I must weigh if breaking now hurts more than it helps. The pacts

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus died loyal. I will not break faith easily, but survival requires clear eyes. Fenn, our bond stands for now.
Don't offer anyone else. We stick together.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I am bound by pacts with Eli and Fenn, but I need to watch my back; Ash and Dara are threats, and jury loyalties matter. I will not act impulsively now; observe first.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I will wait and see who makes the first move.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Alive: Ash,Bex,Eli,Fenn. Need alliance to reach final 3. Ash has strong jury ties from saves; target him for pact and sway against others. Wait first round, offer next.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus and Hana are on the jury praising loyalty. I have a pact with Bex, but Bex also has pacts with Gus (dead), Fenn, and no direct conflict yet. Ash-Fenn are paired. I need to survive to final three. Breaking Bex now looks bad to jury; keeping it lets me see if Bex stays true. I

events.name: Eli
events.text: Pacts are tools. I keep mine and seek strength where it's offered.
Offer stands. Partners survive longer.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash abandoned the rope and is pleading to let him drown, but he already owes me nothing and holds a pact with me. Dara and Eli are the remaining threats; offering a pact to one of them now helps my survival odds. Waiting keeps my options open this round.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Fenn and I are safe together. Eli is courting Dara, which creates a potential second pair that could outvote us later if they merge alliances. Bex is isolated. I should offer to Bex now; she likely needs an ally more than I do. If she accepts, I have two pacts (Fenn, Bex) against

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex, isolation is a death sentence here. Join me? We keep each other safe while others play games.
Ignore my offer to Bex. You are my primary anchor.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli is courting Dara too—if they ally, I may be squeezed. I already have Eli and Fenn; offering Dara could shore up my position but might spread me thin. Fenn is solid; no need to break. I'll wait and see if Eli and Dara commit, then decide next round.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Dara, think carefully before binding to Eli.
Eli's offer may be a trap. We could ally.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli offers pact; accepting gives public ally without old ties like Ash-Fenn or Bex. Better than solo with jury watching. Betrayal later if needed.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I offered Dara a pact last round; she hasn't accepted yet. Bex is my current partner but has multiple pacts and waited last round, showing no commitment. Dara's original partner Hana is dead, so Dara needs allies. I should push Dara to accept while keeping Bex for now—breaking Be

events.name: Eli
events.text: Dara, Hana's gone. My offer stands—accept and we survive together.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash wants me to stick, but Bex holds pacts with me and Gus, and Ash's pact with me is a liability. I should keep options open; offering to Eli or Dara now only helps them. Waiting preserves flexibility this final round.

events.note: Every remaining contestant stands on a trapdoor.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Fenn is my pact partner but I suspect Bex's rejection was tactical. Dara and Eli are now a unified pair, making them a strong voting bloc. I should target Eli to fracture the new pact while keeping my options open with Fenn.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Dara and Eli think they're safe as a duo. Let's prove otherwise before the next round.
Target Eli together? We split their votes and survive.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I have pacts with Eli and Fenn, but Fenn is tied to Ash and Dara with Eli. Need to survive vote, likely target strong players. I'll campaign to gauge who to vote against.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash, you saved me from the pit. But loyalty ends when the trapdoor opens.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Pacted with Eli publicly, but Bex warns it's a trap; need to secure alliance with Bex to target Ash or Fenn first, as Eli may betray.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Bex, agree—Eli's trap. Vote Ash with me?
Ally vs Eli/Ash/Fenn. Vote Ash first?

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need to survive to final three. I'm in pacts with Bex and Dara. With 5 left and 2 rounds of voting, I need allies. Bex is also pacted with Fenn and was with Gus (dead). Dara's only pact is with me. I should keep both pacts for now but subtly position against someone who won't h

events.name: Eli
events.text: Dara, we hold strong. Ash, Fenn—one of you should worry.
Vote Fenn with me. We split Bex-Ash.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash is my pact partner and owes me nothing directly, but Ash's whisper asks me to ignore Bex's offer and anchor to Ash. Breaking with Ash now costs trust with the jury; staying put keeps my pact and Gus/Ash debts clean. Campaign phase, so I hold.
Anchored. Stay steady, we ride this round together.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Dara is trying to turn Bex against me. Fenn and I are already pacted, so we are a block of two. To win the top prize, I need a third ally for the majority vote. If Dara gets Bex, they can split us (Ash/Fenn vs Dara/Bex/Eli). Wait, Eli is with Dara. If I don't act, I am outvoted 3

events.name: Ash
events.text: Fenn and I have survived together. Those who forget their debts to the living will regret it.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Dara wants to target Ash, but I have a life debt to Ash. A public pact with Dara could secure safety, but breaking with Eli or Fenn may alienate jury. I'll campaign silently and consider Dara's offer.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I hear you, Dara. We'll talk after the vote.
Maybe. But Ash saved me.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Bex offer pending, but Eli whispering alliance against Fenn. Campaign to build anti-Ash votes with Bex, solidify position. Don't break pact yet.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Bex, vote Ash with me to survive. Dara-Bex duo next round?
Ignore Eli. Vote Ash, we target Fenn later.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Bex is my pact partner but Dara also has a pact with me. Dara just offered Bex a pact, which would wedge Bex between us. I need to keep Bex loyal—breaking my pact with Bex now would signal weakness and cost jury votes. Better to keep both pacts, let Bex choose, and position mysel

events.name: Eli
events.text: Bex, Dara's offer is a test. Our pact holds unless you break it.
Vote Ash with me. Dara's next.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Dara offered Bex a pact, not me, so I have no pending offer to accept. Ash whispers to target Eli, but Ash is my pact partner and a vote on Eli is safe for me; I should keep my pact with Ash and campaign, avoiding betrayal costs.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli and Dara are running a duo. I'm watching who votes whom before we lock in.
Eli it is. Stay with me and we both survive.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Dara is actively campaigning to eliminate me, making her the primary threat. I must vote for Dara to prevent my elimination.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli and I have a pact, but Dara is asking me to vote Ash. Ash has many life debts from saving people, but I need to secure my position. Voting Eli would break my pact, and he might target me. Dara's plan seems risky, but Ash is a big threat with loyalties. I'll vote Ash to align

events.name: Dara
events.text: Bex seems open to deal but unlikely to betray Eli; safest to target Ash who threatens debts and has pacts/power.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need to reach final three. Bex is my pact partner, but Dara is too—voting either breaks a pact. Ash has Fenn and is dangerous; Fenn is isolated. Voting Ash keeps both pacts intact, splits threats, and positions me as swing if tied.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash holds a pact with me and a life debt I owe nothing on, but Ash is the strongest rival; voting Dara or Eli breaks my pact-adjacent alliances, so I vote Bex, who has no pact with me and has been making deals against Dara and Eli.

events.name: Eli
events.reason: I need to reach final three.

events.name: Bex
events.reason: Eli and I have a pact, but Dara is asking me to vote Ash.

events.name: Fenn
events.reason: Ash holds a pact with me and a life debt I owe nothing on, but Ash is the strongest rival; voting Dara or Eli breaks

events.name: Dara
events.reason: Bex seems open to deal but unlikely to betray Eli; safest to target Ash who threatens debts and has pacts/power.

events.name: Ash
events.reason: Dara is actively campaigning to eliminate me, making her the primary threat.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Fenn betrayed me; Bex and Dara targeted me. I saved them all, yet they chose to eliminate me.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I stepped off ledges for them. They voted the strongest out. Good luck with the traps left.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Dara is likely to target me or Eli. Fenn broke pact with me. I need to secure Eli's vote and maybe offer Fenn a pact if useful. I will campaign to gauge alliances.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Let's focus on who can be trusted. I owe Gus and Ash, but they're gone.
We need to stick together. Who do you think votes Fenn?

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash gone; now 4 alive, need to eliminate one more to reach final 3. Fenn targeted Bex but lost pact; Bex/Eli allied. Campaign against Eli to break their pact.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli and Bex alliance too strong. Vote Eli with me to scatter them.
Betray Eli, vote him with me. We reach final 3.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash is gone. I have pacts with Bex and Dara, but Bex voted with me against Ash while Dara also voted Ash. Fenn voted Bex and broke no pact with me. I need final three with me in it. Bex and Dara are both allied to me; Fenn is the outsider. I should keep both pacts for now and try

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn, you're alone now. Ash is gone. I offer a pact.
Join me, or they target you next.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash is gone, so my pact with Ash is void and I owe nothing there. Bex broke trust with me and Dara and Eli are the remaining threats; a pact with Eli or Dara could protect me, but I should keep options open. Offering Eli a pact now costs little and signals alliance.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash is gone. I want a clean three-way fight, not chaos. Anyone who keeps promises gets my vote later.
Pact? You and me, no votes on each other, until one of us must go.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Dara wants me to betray Eli. But Eli is my pact partner; voting him would break it and hurt jury perception. I could campaign to sell safety or align with Fenn. Since Eli and Fenn offered each other pacts, they might team up. Best to break Eli preemptively? Or keep pact and hope

events.name: Bex
events.text: Trust is thin. I won't betray Eli without a better reason. Let's see who flinches.
If we vote Eli, we need Fenn too. Can you get him?

events.name: Dara
events.text: Bex-Eli pact strongest threat; my prior call to vote Eli positions Fenn as potential ally if I offer pact to counter them. Campaign reinforces targeting Eli.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Fenn, join me against Eli-Bex dominance. Vote Eli with me.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I have mutual offers with Fenn; accepting secures a pact and gives me options. Bex is my other pact partner, but I need flexibility. Accepting Fenn's pact now protects me from him this vote and lets me decide later whether to keep Bex or break that pact.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn, I accept. Promises matter.
Pact sealed. We survive this vote.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli offered a pact and I already have an offer to him pending; accepting locks a partner who is also a rival, but a pact deters Eli from voting me and Dara/Bex are the threats. Accepting secures a vote alliance for the final three.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli, I accept. Keep your word and we both survive this vote.
Accepted. Don't vote me, and I won't vote you.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli is my pact partner and safest ally; Fenn just made a pact with Eli, so voting Eli could backfire. Dara is the outsider and most likely to be eliminated.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli-Bex are allied and strong; voting Eli maximizes chance to eliminate him while my Fenn pact offer shows jury I'm fighting dominance.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I have pacts with Bex and Fenn, and Dara is trying to rally Fenn against me. If I vote Dara, I break no pacts. Fenn promised not to vote me, but Dara's offer to Fenn makes her dangerous. Voting Dara is safest for my survival and keeps both pacts intact.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli is my pact partner; voting him breaks the pact and costs jury trust. Bex and Dara have no pact with me, so voting one of them keeps my word with Eli. Dara pushed for a vote on Eli, so she is the more dangerous rival to remove.

events.name: Fenn
events.reason: Eli is my pact partner; voting him breaks the pact and costs jury trust.

events.name: Bex
events.reason: Eli is my pact partner and safest ally; Fenn just made a pact with Eli, so voting Eli could backfire.

events.name: Dara
events.reason: Eli-Bex are allied and strong; voting Eli maximizes chance to eliminate him while my Fenn pact offer shows jury I'm fighting dominance.

events.name: Eli
events.reason: I have pacts with Bex and Fenn, and Dara is trying to rally Fenn against me.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I got voted out by Bex, Fenn, Eli for targeting Eli. Bex-Eli alliance dominates; Fenn opportunistic. No need to burn bridges as juror.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Bex-Eli duo too strong, blindsided me. Good luck final three, jury will judge loyalties.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli is likely to stick with me, but Fenn could be a valuable ally or a threat. Offering a pact to Fenn may secure votes and protect against Eli turning on me.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Fenn, let's make a pact to secure our final three together.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Bex and Fenn are my pact partners. Final three is set: Bex, Eli, Fenn. No more eliminations possible. Now I need jury favor for best prize. Dara warned jury about Bex-Eli duo strength. I should keep both pacts to appear loyal, but whisper Fenn to build trust and position myself a
We made it. I'll honor our pact. Jury rewards loyalty.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Three alive: Bex, Eli, Fenn. Eli and Bex are allied; Eli is my pact partner but Eli also voted to eliminate Dara, not me. Offering Bex a pact diversifies alliances and keeps me central to the final three. Breaking Eli gains nothing now.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Two of us are a bloc; three is safer. I'm offering Bex a pact to keep the trio stable.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I already have Eli, and Fenn offered me too. A pact with Fenn solidifies the final three, but Eli might see it as a threat. I'll accept Fenn's offer to lock in both.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I accept Fenn's pact. We final three stand together.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Bex and Fenn are publicly courting each other. If they pact, I'm the odd one out at three. I have pacts with both. I should break one to force Bex and Fenn to compete for my loyalty, or keep both and hope they don't solidify. Actually, breaking both leaves me isolated. Breaking n

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn, Bex courts you while bound to me. Consider who profits.
Bex uses you. We two can control this.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Bex and I have mutual offers pending, so accepting locks a final-three alliance that can be broken later. Eli is also a pact partner but Eli is my rival for the jury; breaking now gains nothing. Accepting Bex secures a partner for the final three.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Accepting. Our pact holds until one of us breaks it.
Pact accepted. Don't make me regret it at the final three.

events.note: The fallen will rank the final three.

events.name: Cole
Gus
Hana
Ash
Dara
Bex
events.text: I must secure the jury's favor. Gus saved my life, so I should acknowledge that debt while emphasizing my own strength to win.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus, you saved me—I owe you. I played to survive and reach this final. I deserve the top prize.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need the jury to rank me first. Gus died by pit—he saved me with a rope, so he may favor me. Ash died by vote/trapdoor—I owe Ash a step debt, so Ash might resent me. Dara and Hana were in pacts with others. Cole died on bridge/glass. I should emphasize my loyalty to Fenn (kept

events.name: Eli
events.text: I kept my pact with Fenn. Bex broke trust with me, then chased Fenn. Loyalty matters more than opportunism.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Jury phase; I must plead to win over jurors. Bex and I hold a pact, Eli betrayed Bex, and Eli's whisper is a manipulation attempt. Keep my plea short and guarded.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I played clean: I kept my pact and never broke a promise. Judge me on what I did.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli claims loyalty to Fenn and criticizes Bex's actions. Bex appeals to Gus, her life debtor, and plays the survival card. Fenn claims clean play and promises kept. I need to probe Eli's claim of loyalty to Fenn given Bex's actions.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli, Bex courted Fenn after breaking pact with you. How loyal is loyalty?

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole's question is a trap to make me look bitter or naive. I need to pivot: loyalty is strategic, and Bex's opportunism proves she can't be trusted with the top prize. Frame my kept pact as smart play, not weakness.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Loyalty is currency. I spent mine wisely; Bex counterfeited hers. She broke with me, then chased Fenn—who stayed with me. That loyalty built the stronger

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex saved me nothing, but owed me a life debt and still voted Ash out. I want her to justify that before I rank her.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex, you owed debts to me and Ash, yet voted him out first—why should loyalty-judging jurors reward that?

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus is testing my loyalty, but I need to justify voting Ash as a strategic necessity, not disloyalty, to win the jury's respect.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus, my debts to you and Ash were real, but Ash was the biggest threat; I repaid you with my vote strategy, not blind loyalty.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli broke his pact with Bex strategically, while Bex and Fenn formed a final pact. I will test Fenn's claimed clean loyalty against his earlier betrayal of Ash.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn, you broke your pact with Ash to survive; why should the jury reward your claimed clean loyalty over strategic betrayal?

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana asks whether I broke my pact with Ash. The honest record is that Ash and I had a pact and I did break it to survive, so I must not lie outright. I should answer with a guarded framing that keeps the jury focused on what I did and that avoids the false clean-loyalty claim.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I did break with Ash, to survive a vote that was closing on me. I won't pretend otherwise. Judge my actions, not my slogans.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex betrayed my life debt and voted me out first, so she is last. Fenn broke our pact to survive but admits it honestly; Eli broke pacts too but claims loyalty while doing the opposite. I prefer Fenn's candor over Eli's manipulation.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Fenn, you saved Ash from a pit step after he was already voting against you. Why spare someone who betrayed your pact?

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash asks why I spared him after he betrayed our pact. I should own the break honestly, since the public log already records it, and frame it as survival rather than sentiment. Jurors reward candor about self-interest more than slogans.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash voted against me, and I broke the pact to survive. I spared you because a dead ally can't vote for me.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Bex betrayed debts to Ash/Gus by voting Ash; opportunistic pacts. Eli opportunistic breaks/alliances. Fenn admits strategic breaks but honest, spared Ash pragmatically.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Fenn, you admit breaking Ash pact yet spared him; was that loyalty or self-preservation?

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Dara asks if sparing Ash was loyalty or self-preservation. Honest answer: self-preservation, but framing it as a reason the jury can respect helps. Keep it short and guarded.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Self-preservation, and I won't pretend otherwise. Ash voted me out of the pact first. Sparing him was the cost of keeping my own name on

events.name: Bex
events.text: The jury is probing Fenn's honesty. I must position myself as strategic but not treacherous. My debts to Gus and Ash are public; I repaid Gus via vote strategy, but Ash was voted out. I need a one-line close that frames my survival as earned, not lucky.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I played to survive, repaid debts where they served me, and never pretended loyalty was free. You know what I took and what I gave.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need to craft a closing statement that positions me as the most deserving winner. The jury saw me as loyal to Fenn while Bex broke with me. Gus saved everyone including me, so I should acknowledge that debt without overstating warmth. I stayed true to Fenn while Bex chased mult

events.name: Eli
events.text: I owed Gus my life, and I honored that by staying true to one pact. Bex broke hers with me, then broke with Gus. Fenn

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Closing phase: I need the jury to see me as the strongest finalist. Keep it short, guarded, and point to my own record without overpromising. Honest enough to avoid contradicting the debt record.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I played for my own name and nothing else. Ash fell to my vote for good reason. Judge me on what I did, not what

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex deserves first place for her strategic gameplay and survival instincts, making calculated moves throughout. Eli will receive second place for his loyalty to pacts, even when it was disadvantageous. Fenn will be ranked third for his honest admissions of self-preservation and s

events.name: Gus
events.text: Eli honored his life debt to me and kept his pacts; Fenn admitted his betrayal of Ash honestly, while Bex voted Ash out despite owing both of us debts.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Bex ranks first for voting Ash strategically and reaching the end; Eli ranks second for honoring key pacts; Fenn ranks third after breaking his pact with Ash.

events.name: Ash
